Name: Amanda Rowe
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

I would start this by using the textbook pages that students are used to already seeing. I think I would set requirements such as a number of annotations per page, or every picture there must be a thought from the student. I see this as students annotating as they read certain pages, then a They say/ I say summary more at the end of the required pages.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

I think for Sped students I would only have them fill in one part of the they say or I say. So as the teacher I might go ahead and summarize the "they say" portion to see how the students respond or connect to the " I say" piece.

I could also see using this as students only doing they " They say" piece to check for understanding of the material before they are allowed to do the I say - chunk it into smaller pieces to make sure students are getting the information you intended for them to understand thought out the reading. I also vocabulary words or words they don't know would be a good variation of annotation that students could do to also show the connections or mis concepts that are happening why they are reading.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

I really this like strategy. I think it forces students to understand one perspective while then forming their own opinion as to agree/disagree or on the same lines as what the information was telling them.
